title: ApplyOps
description: INPUT of `dmtool -m <model> apply <ops.json>` (CLI-SPEC §7) — an ORDERED array of op-records applied to ONE model in a single session: one read → ordered surgery → one terminal kernel gate → one write, with atomic rollback (a mid-sequence failure writes nothing). Each op-record is {target, op, …args}; the per-op fields are that verb's params — discover them from `manifest` + `schema <target> <op>`. The locator key for an EXISTING element matches the standalone verb's positional: a path-located element uses `<element>PathInModel` (`fieldPathInModel` / `groupPathInModel` / `rulePathInModel` / `computationPathInModel`), a typedef `typeDefId`, an include `alias`. (`rule add` / `computation add` instead carry the NEW element inline — `field`/`code`/`condition`/`messages` for a rule — with no path.) A `rule modify` op edits any of condition / severity / messages / metadata (annotation·remove-annotation·internal-description·external-description·remove-internal-description·remove-external-description — the rule peer of `group modify`'s metadata; rules have no label) (≥1); messages MERGE per locale so a one-locale edit keeps the rest, and `rule add` accepts the same metadata keys at add time. A REPEATABLE key (a CLI flag the manifest marks `kind:SCALAR` because it repeats — `add-locale`/`remove-locale`/`role`) takes a JSON array in an op-record (`add-locale:["de_DE"]`), but a bare scalar (`add-locale:"de_DE"`) also binds (treated as a 1-element list). The op-set spans add·modify·remove·read PLUS the reference-rewriting refactors: `field`/`group` rename·move, `rule` rename, `typedef` rename (each runs its §6 safety gate at its turn against the live model — a refused refactor rolls the whole sequence back). A `group remove` takes the same `cascade` safe-delete gate as the standalone verb (a group still referenced from outside its subtree is refused unless `cascade:true`); `rule remove` deletes a rule. `extract`/`inline` stay standalone verbs. An op-record carries the SAME settable flags its standalone verb advertises (manifest-derived, parity-guarded): an `include add` op accepts `repeatability` (mount a repeating sub-form) and `exclude-rules`/`exclude-computations`; a `config modify` op accepts `supported-character` (a repeatable key that REPLACES the allowed-character set, like the flag). An unsupported target/op self-corrects via RK_UNKNOWN_OP, which lists the ops apply DOES support. Distinct from `batch` (which takes {verb, args} for stateless per-op dispatch). Each op emits a per-op result envelope (a successful edit is `staged`/`written:false` until the terminal gate commits the whole sequence — the write is ATOMIC at the wrapper, not per op, so a per-op `written:false` is NOT a failure); the wrapper is {ops, committed, summary, failedAt, written, results[]}, where `committed`/`written` + the human `summary` are the authoritative net-effect signals (read those, not the per-op flags).

target.description: the element family acted on: field | group | rule | … (see `manifest`)

op.description: the operation: add | modify | remove | read | rename | move (valid for the target; see `manifest`)

time-zone.description: for config modify: absence defaults UTC; exact UTC, GMT, Europe/Berlin are interpreter-supported; another kernel-valid Java id is accepted with an evaluator-scope warning; blank/unknown ids are rejected

supported-character.description: for config modify: one singleton BMP character, inclusive x-y range, or atomic combined grapheme per entry; an empty/absent model list selects the full BMP excluding surrogates (not supplementary-plane characters)
